Hi Markus,

Quick intro — Elena at CloudBroker (we're the reseller handling deals for several MSPs). We're shaping a combined AWS+GCP private offer for a customer and need clarity on how Redwood handles:

- Passback routing (which party gets the cloud marketplace passback and how it's split between AWS/GCP).
- Recommended partner margin (we need the % to include in the reseller agreement).
- Invoice routing and whether Redwood can emit a single consolidated invoice for both clouds to our end customer (we currently get separate marketplace credits).

Can you share the passback template you typically use and any notes on tax handling or invoice flow? The customer is asking for a single PO and a reseller-friendly routing.

I've attached our template that shows what the buyer expects (attachment: requested_template_stub.xlsx).

Elena — thanks for the note and the template. High level response now, attaching our standard passback mapping and a reseller agreement draft in the follow-up email.

Short answers:
1) Passback routing: Redwood can support partner passback routed to CloudBroker for both AWS and GCP private offers. We normally map passback at the SKU level so the cloud provider's marketplace rebate is passed to the reseller entity you register.

2) Partner margin: we typically leave negotiation of margin to you/the buyer, but operationally our common signal is a 10–18% margin band for resellers on combined private offers (depends on committed volume/term).

3) Invoicing: Redwood can emit invoices to either the end customer or to the reseller (CloudBroker) depending on PO and contract setup. If you want a single consolidated invoice across clouds we need a consolidated billing ID and the reseller entity must be set as the bill-to in both clouds. We'll need evidence (PO + signed reseller agreement).

Couple of clarification Qs so we give concrete numbers:
- Will CloudBroker be the legal reseller (bill-to) on both AWS and GCP marketplace entries?
- Is the customer asking for list-price consolidation (we can provide a waterfall that preserves vendor list price and shows passback splits) or a net-fee model?

Cc'ing Ben (pricing) and Irene (ops) to add specifics and share the passback template. If we get confirmation on legal entity and desired invoice flow I can circulate a final passback schedule and a DocuSign link for the reseller agreement.

Best,
Markus Klein

Markus / Irene — quick pricing scaffolding for CloudBroker to consider (putting the earlier notes into an operational waterfall).

On Tue, May 19, 2026 at 10:18 AM markus.klein@redwood.com wrote:
> Elena — thanks for the note and the template...

Proposal (example waterfall):
- Step 1: Start from provider marketplace credit at SKU level (AWS credit, GCP credit).
- Step 2: Provider passback routed 100% to the reseller entity (CloudBroker) per marketplace rules.
- Step 3: Redwood applies a per-SKU management fee (negotiable); common band: 2–4%.
- Step 4: Remaining pooled amount allocated to CloudBroker as passback. CloudBroker and customer can then apply their margin.

Suggested default margin framing for reseller agreement (you can change):
- Standard: 12% of list for combined offers (term 1 year, minimal commit).
- Volume incentive: 16% if commit >= $500k ARR.
- High-commit: 18% for multi-year strategic deals.

Tax/invoice notes:
- If CloudBroker wants consolidated invoice to the customer we need billing linkage set in each marketplace entry and a single remit address. That will allow us to present one consolidated Redwood invoice (we will still report per-cloud passbacks for audit).
- Cross-border tax: if reseller is outside US, we may need to issue vendor-specific tax exhibits; ops will confirm.

Attachments to include in a follow-up: a passback mapping workbook and a redline reseller agreement draft.
